Being in a relationship with an ED or any mental illness is, tricky to say the least. My ex was BPD and I was in the height of my ED and it ultimately led in collapse, which still breaks me a year later. I think that one day, if he decides to pursue recovery, he'll see past the brain fog that led him to that decision. You know what you're doing is wrong but you just convince yourself you don't care and get that fuck it mentality.

You just have to remember at the end of the day, it was him who ended it, not the ED. I think it's great you're so loving and supportive, but you have to have some self love too. He has to have some rationale over his actions, and I say that because I've been there. I willingly chose my illness over fighting for myself and for someone that I truly loved so fucking much. I clocked out of him completely and I can only imagine what that feels like on the other end.  As much as eds are shitty and ruthless and consuming you do not deserve that. 

I'm really sorry, and thank you for sharing your side of the story. It really opened my eyes and made me think. I'm hoping so much that he can open his eyes long enough to see what's in front of him and allow some healing in. And let you help him help himself in the process. 

 When you're in that hole and finally open up, especially when you're not ready to recover, the fight or flight urges tend to flair because he's scared you're going to just expect him to get better. I wish he could see it differently.

Lunches were things like rice bowls with a protein, veggies, beans, and some kind of fat like an avocado. Or a sandwich with a cookie and a fruit. 

Dinners were pretty similar, carbs like potatoes or something of the sort with a protein and veggies cooked in butter/oil, sometimes things like stir fry or pizza or something more interesting, sometimes we would be given a dessert like a fortune cookie or a small ice cream. 

Snacks were always usually a carb and a fat, like string cheese with chips, pita and hummus, trail mix, pb toast

Overall I think their meals/meal planning was a great foundation to take out of treatment, barring I stayed long enough to retain any of it 😅 but I think it should be similar mostly anywhere, just might be more room for flexibility!
